newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS - Rolling Nov index positions.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS - Rolling Nov index positions.

text.p: Open interest in November stock index options, particularly puts, remained high Thursday, one day before the options expire but investors were rolling positions out to longer maturities, traders said.
"What I've seen in the OEX (S&P 100 index) has been all rolls," one trader said.
"The ones left tend to be deeper in-the-money because of the upside motion" in the underlying market, he said.
At 1215 CST/1815 GMT, OEX was up more than three points at about 711, just below its session high.
Traders said that before Thursday, roll activity was thin, with few expirations.
Among the options, the November 710 puts, down 1-15/16 at 1-13/16, were most active, with turnover of about 19,400. Open interest was 11,318, including an addition of 3,874 Wednesday.
The corresponding call rose 1-1/2 at 3-1/2. It traded 18,375 contracts. Open interest was 17,927, with an addition of 1,353 Wednesday.
Among November OEX puts, open interest was high from the 680 through the 710. On the call side, open interest was high in the 700, 705, 710 and 715 strikes.
The broader S&P 500 index .SPX, was up 2.6 points at nearly 734. It reached an intraday high of 735.31, a record.
Among SPX options traded on Chicago Board Options Exchange, the heaviest trading was being done in the December series, led by the December 725 put, which traded about 18,000 contracts.
The December 725 put, which had open interest of 18,271, was down 2-1/8 at 6-1/2.
Ohter active December SPX options included the December 725 call, the December 740 call and the December 735 put.
